claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: The narrative identifies the evidence as a social media post written by Albert, which qualifies as a statement made outside of the current trial or hearing.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) requires the statement to be made out of court to constitute hearsay.
arguments.evidence_span: a social media post written by Albert

arguments.text: The post describes Taylor Swift as Albert's favorite artist, which constitutes a clear assertion of fact or opinion regarding Albert's personal preference.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(a) defines a statement as an oral or written assertion intended by the person as an assertion.
arguments.evidence_span: describing Taylor as his favorite artist

arguments.text: The post is introduced specifically on the issue of whether Albert liked Taylor Swift, indicating it is being offered to prove the truth of that preference.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) defines hearsay as a statement offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted in the statement.
arguments.evidence_span: On the issue of whether Albert liked Taylor Swift

arguments.text: The narrative does not indicate the post is offered for any non-hearsay purpose (e.g., notice, effect on listener, impeachment) nor does it fall under a FRE 801(d)(2) exclusion.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) applies only when a statement is offered for its truth and does not fall under an exclusion or exception.
